Ibrahim Hassan (Director of Data) is operationally distracted by an internal migration and has an auto-reply limiting availability through September, leaving the pre-renewal review unscheduled during the most critical engagement window. Zero support tickets compound the signal: this is not smooth operations, it is disengagement without complaint, which is the most dangerous churn pattern.

leverage_points.what: Send Ibrahim Hassan a direct, concise executive-level email (not a newsletter, not a generic check-in) referencing the migration context and requesting a 20-minute call in the next two weeks to 'make sure we're set up to support Northwind through the transition and into renewal'
leverage_points.why: Hassan's auto-reply signals he is filtering low-priority outreach; a targeted, peer-level message that acknowledges his migration workload and frames the conversation as support — not sales — is the only format likely to cut through before the window closes further

leverage_points.what: Conduct a usage diagnostic call with Hassan or his delegate: map which of the original 41 users dropped off, whether the migration displaced workflows that used your product, and whether the remaining 15 active users are the right ones or just stragglers
leverage_points.why: The 63% drop is a fact; its cause is unknown. Without diagnosing whether the drop is migration-related (temporary), structural (permanent workflow change), or competitive (replacement tool being evaluated), no retention play can be constructed — and the AE's complacency assumption will persist by default

leverage_points.what: Build a re-adoption plan targeting the gap between 15 and 50 licensed users, tied explicitly to post-migration workflow needs; present it to Hassan as a renewal-aligned roadmap with a clear value milestone before contract date
leverage_points.why: With 100 days to renewal, there is still time to demonstrate recovery if the cause of drop-off is diagnosed quickly. A structured re-adoption plan signals investment in the account and gives Hassan a concrete reason to renew at current ARR rather than downgrade or churn

brief.do_this_today: Draft and send a direct email to Ibrahim Hassan today — subject line referencing the migration specifically (e.g., 'Supporting Northwind through the migration + renewal prep') — that (1) acknowledges he's heads-down, (2) offers a 20-minute call at his convenience before end of September, and (3) positions the conversation as ensuring the product is configured to serve his team's post-migration needs. Do not mention usage numbers or renewal pressure in this first touch.

contact_persona.comm_style: Signals a preference for low-interruption, asynchronous communication given the auto-reply and limited availability declaration; likely responds to concise, substantive outreach that respects his time and operational context rather than relationship-building small talk
contact_persona.decision_style: Data-oriented by role (Director of Data); likely makes decisions based on operational fit and team utility rather than relationship loyalty. Currently in a high-cognitive-load period (migration), so decisions are probably being deferred or delegated unless flagged as urgent
contact_persona.what_they_say_vs_mean: The auto-reply and limited availability message says 'I'm busy until September' but means 'don't interrupt me unless it matters.' The absence of complaints does not mean satisfaction — it means the product has faded from his attention entirely, which is a pre-churn posture, not a stable one
contact_persona.approach_recommendation: Do not pitch. Do not send templated outreach. Reach Hassan with a single, short, high-signal message that demonstrates you understand his migration context and frames the conversation as your team serving his needs — not securing a renewal. If he doesn't respond, identify a delegate within his team among the remaining 15 active users who can confirm whether the product still has a post-migration role.

secondary_contacts.name_title: Unknown — day-to-day admin or active user (identity not surfaced in available data)
secondary_contacts.note: The 15 remaining weekly active users represent the only live touchpoint with the account; identifying who among them is a power user or team lead could provide an internal champion or at minimum a diagnostic contact if Hassan remains unresponsive through September

data_gaps: Identity and role of the remaining 15 active users — are they core team or peripheral, and is any one of them a potential internal champion?
Root cause of migration: what system is being migrated, and does it intersect with workflows that previously drove product usage?
Whether competitor tools are being evaluated or trialed during the migration window
Hassan's historical responsiveness pattern prior to the migration — was he ever an engaged contact or always arm's-length?
Whether the AE has any direct relationship with Hassan or other Northwind leadership that could be leveraged for an executive-to-executive reach-out
brief.confidence_note: Usage data is unambiguous and high-confidence; the risk type and severity are clear. Confidence is capped at medium because Hassan's internal intent is entirely unknown — there is no QBR transcript, no direct conversation log, and no sentiment signal beyond the auto-reply. A single 20-minute diagnostic call would shift this to high confidence and enable a targeted retention play.
suggested_questions: When the migration completes, which workflows does your team plan to run through our platform versus what has shifted to the new environment?
Of the team members who were active on the platform earlier this year, are they paused due to the migration or have their roles changed?
What would a successful first 30 days post-migration look like for your data team, and how can we make sure we're configured to support that?

brief.situation: Corvid Media is a healthy, high-adoption base account (40 seats, 92% WAU, NPS 61) with a confirmed renewal on 1 December 2026 and no churn signals. Marcus has given an explicit October re-engagement date, signaling conditional interest rather than rejection; the editorial team's active use and internal nickname for the dashboard ('the morning read') confirms genuine product value and user-side pull for the expansion.

leverage_points.why: Marcus gave a specific revisit date—October—which is a commitment, not a soft brush-off. Arriving prepared with a tight ROI narrative tied to actual usage data keeps the expansion alive without pressuring him during the freeze.

leverage_points.what: Identify and quietly map the editorial team members who are already asking about Audience Insights; document their use cases and build a one-page internal brief to hand Marcus in October.
leverage_points.why: The CRM notes flag a communication gap between editorial power users and the budget holder. Bridging that gap with concrete, bottom-up demand evidence gives Marcus internal cover to approve the expansion once Finance lifts the freeze.

leverage_points.what: Prepare a bundled October proposal that packages the Audience Insights module and 25 sales seats with a multi-year or early-commit incentive timed to align with post-reorg budget cycles.
leverage_points.why: The reorg is expected to settle before October; positioning a deal with a financial sweetener at exactly the moment new budget is accessible maximizes conversion probability and ties expansion to renewal momentum (renewal is 1 December, only ~60 days after the October window).

brief.do_this_today: Block a calendar reminder for the first week of October to re-engage Marcus, and send a brief, no-ask check-in email this week acknowledging the freeze, confirming you'll return in October, and attaching one data point on the editorial team's current usage—keeping the thread warm without creating pressure.

contact_persona.comm_style: Professional and decisive; communicates in clear, bounded statements ('Not this quarter… Come back in October'). Low noise, high signal—does not over-explain or hedge. Prefers concise, structured interactions.
contact_persona.decision_style: Finance-constrained and process-respecting; defers to organizational guardrails rather than making discretionary calls under uncertainty. Not risk-averse by nature—he presented the expansion proposal context clearly—but will not override a freeze. Likely an analytical buyer who needs business justification aligned with budget cycles.
contact_persona.what_they_say_vs_mean: Says 'not this quarter' — means 'yes in principle, but I need the organizational constraint removed first.' The explicit October date is a soft commitment, not a dodge; he is managing upward to Finance, not stalling the vendor.
contact_persona.approach_recommendation: Return in October with a tight, pre-built business case using the editorial team's organic demand as internal proof points. Do not re-pitch from scratch—reference the July conversation explicitly to signal you respected his timeline. Lead with ROI and user evidence, not features. Keep the meeting short and decision-ready; Marcus will not want to re-litigate the product story.

secondary_contacts.note: Day-to-day power users who have already expressed interest in the Audience Insights module; they are the source of bottom-up demand but lack budget authority. Valuable as internal advocates and proof-point generators to support Marcus's eventual approval.

data_gaps: Identity and title of the editorial team members asking about Audience Insights—needed to assess their influence on Marcus and their value as internal champions
Current status of the internal reorg: is it on track to resolve before October, or could the freeze extend?
Whether the sales team expansion (+25 seats) was internally requested by sales leadership or proposed solely by the CSM—determines how much internal pull exists beyond editorial
Finance decision-maker identity: who actually controls the freeze, and does Marcus have any discretionary budget headroom?
NPS verbatim comments—NPS 61 is positive but knowing what drives it would sharpen the October value narrative
brief.confidence_note: Base health signals are strong and the situation is clear, but only two source types are available (annual review deck plus CRM/email summaries). Confidence would increase with direct access to the full email thread, any Slack texture from the editorial team, and a clearer picture of the reorg timeline and Finance stakeholder.
suggested_questions: Marcus, now that we're approaching October—has the reorg settled enough for Finance to reopen new spend, or should we plan for a slightly later conversation?
Which members of the editorial team have been most vocal about Audience Insights, and would it be useful for us to put together a brief showing how they'd use it before we meet?

When you think about the sales team expansion, was that driven by a request from sales leadership, or is that something you're proposing on their behalf—and does that change how you'd want to frame the business case internally?

leverage_points.why: Raj is the operational champion for the 2 satisfied users; locking in documented value for the users who are actually engaged protects against further decay and gives Hannah evidence-based justification to maintain even a reduced subscription

leverage_points.what: Build a reactivation trigger into the account plan tied to Ashgrove's next hiring cycle or team expansion, with a lightweight expansion proposal ready to send when headcount recovers
leverage_points.why: The reorg is the root cause of the footprint reduction, not product dissatisfaction — if Ashgrove rebuilds the platform team, the expansion opportunity reopens; planting this seed now avoids starting from zero later

brief.do_this_today: Send Hannah a concise email (3 bullet points max) confirming the starter-tier proposal is in progress, acknowledging the reorg context without pushback, and setting a specific date for the follow-up proposal delivery — this keeps momentum and signals respect for her stated preference.

contact_persona.comm_style: Direct and candid; she stated her position plainly on the call without hedging. She does not appear to be testing the CSM — what she says is close to what she means. Low tolerance for over-engineered responses or sales pressure.
contact_persona.decision_style: Pragmatic and capacity-driven; her decisions are shaped by team bandwidth and organizational context rather than product sentiment. contact_persona.what_they_say_vs_mean: Says 'I don't have the energy to fight for re-engagement this year' — means 'the org context has taken this off the table and I need a vendor who accepts that rather than pushes back.' contact_persona.approach_recommendation: Lead with empathy for the reorg, validate the right-sizing decision explicitly, and present the starter-tier proposal as a logical and well-supported outcome rather than a consolation prize. Do not pitch expansion or re-engagement of the disengaged users right now — that will read as tone-deaf. Earn trust by making this renewal easy, then plant a quiet seed about future growth when the relationship is stable.

secondary_contacts.note: Day-to-day team lead or senior user who represents the 2 actively engaged engineers; he is the operational champion and the voice of product satisfaction on the account. data_gaps: Raj's full name and title — he appears to be a key operational champion but is incompletely identified
Root cause of the 2 disengaged users reverting to spreadsheets — product gap, onboarding failure, or simply role change post-reorg
Hannah's budget ceiling for the starter tier — knowing the price sensitivity floor would sharpen the proposal

Contract terms and any downgrade penalties that could complicate the right-sizing conversation

A longer CRM history, QBR notes, or usage data would confirm whether the adoption gap predates the reorg or was caused by it, and would sharpen the severity and recommended approach.
